simple_definition: The roadmap's neutral name for side-by-side chips linked through a denser-than-normal layer (organic for 2DO, silicon/glass bridge or interposer for 2DS), replacing loose labels like '2.5D'.
technical_definition: IEEE HIR 2024 ch.22 nomenclature: 2D enhanced = laterally placed dies with a high-density medium between die and substrate; 2DO organic, 2DS inorganic; 3D = dies stacked directly.

simple_definition: Samsung Foundry's brand names for its 2.5D (I-Cube, H-Cube) and 3D (X-Cube) packaging.
technical_definition: I-CubeS: silicon interposer; I-CubeE: embedded silicon bridges in fan-out panel RDL interposer; H-Cube: hybrid ABF+HDI substrate; X-Cube: 3D stacking by micro-bump or Cu hybrid bonding.

simple_definition: Putting the optical (laser-light) data link inside the chip package instead of a plug-in module at the edge of the board, to save power.
technical_definition: Integration of photonic engines with switch/compute dies on the package substrate; TSMC's COUPE stacks an electronic die on a photonic die via SoIC and enters production on substrate in 2026.

simple_definition: How precisely each new layer of a chip lines up on top of the layers already printed.
technical_definition: Layer-to-layer alignment error of patterned features, typically specified in nm (e.g. ~0.7 nm claimed for EXE:5200B).

simple_definition: How many silicon wafers a lithography machine can expose in one hour; the main measure of its productivity.
technical_definition: Scanner throughput at a specified dose and field layout under the acceptance-test protocol (ATP); e.g. 220 wph NXE:3800E, 175 wph EXE:5200B.

simple_definition: A lithography machine that prints a chip pattern by sweeping a slit of light across the mask and wafer at the same time, then stepping to the next spot.
technical_definition: Step-and-scan exposure tool in which reticle and wafer stages move synchronously under a slit-shaped illumination field; standard for KrF, ArF, ArFi and EUV.

simple_definition: An older, simpler kind of lithography machine that exposes one whole chip area at a time and then moves (steps) to the next.
technical_definition: Step-and-repeat projection exposure tool exposing a full field at once; still common for i-line and packaging lithography.

simple_definition: The set of lenses or mirrors inside a lithography machine that shrinks the mask pattern and focuses it onto the wafer.
technical_definition: The projection optics (and associated illumination) module of a lithography system; for ASML supplied solely by Carl Zeiss SMT.

simple_definition: A very powerful laser that hits tiny drops of tin so they glow with the extreme ultraviolet light used in EUV machines.
technical_definition: Pulsed CO2 laser system (multi-stage amplifier, tens of kW average pulse power) used in laser-produced-plasma EUV sources; built by TRUMPF for ASML.

simple_definition: A gas laser that produces deep-ultraviolet light; it is the light source in DUV lithography machines.
technical_definition: Pulsed gas-discharge laser using rare-gas halide mixtures: KrF (248 nm) or ArF (193 nm); made by Cymer (ASML) and Gigaphoton (Komatsu).

simple_definition: Printing one very fine layer in two or more exposure steps because a single exposure cannot make features that small.
technical_definition: Splitting a layer's pattern across several litho-etch (or spacer) steps to beat a tool's single-exposure resolution; EUV and High-NA aim to replace some of these steps with one exposure.

simple_definition: Optics that shrink the mask image by different amounts in the two directions, used in High-NA EUV so existing mask sizes still work.
technical_definition: Projection optics with unequal demagnification (4x and 8x) in High-NA EUV, halving the exposure field and requiring field stitching for large dies.

simple_definition: A way of making chip patterns by pressing a patterned stamp into a soft coating on the wafer, instead of printing with light.
technical_definition: Jet-and-flash imprint of a template into resist, cured and released; Canon's FPA-1200NZ2C claims 14 nm minimum linewidth.

simple_definition: Lithography using 365-nanometre ultraviolet light from mercury lamps, for chips or layers that do not need very small features.
technical_definition: 365 nm mercury-lamp exposure (ASML lists ~220 nm resolution); dominant in power devices, MEMS, sensors and packaging.

simple_definition: Deep-ultraviolet lithography using 248-nanometre light from a krypton-fluoride laser.
technical_definition: 248 nm excimer-laser lithography (ASML lists ~80 nm resolution); used for mid-critical layers, notably in memory.

simple_definition: The most advanced kind of deep-ultraviolet lithography: 193-nanometre laser light with a thin layer of water between lens and wafer to print finer features.
technical_definition: 193 nm ArF excimer lithography with water immersion (NA up to 1.35, ~38 nm single-exposure resolution); ASML's NXT platform.

simple_definition: Testing a lithography machine at the maker's factory to prove it meets the agreed specification before it is shipped.
technical_definition: Pre-shipment test of an integrated system against contractual specs; ASML re-tests at site acceptance (SAT) after installation and recognises revenue at FAT for proven technologies.

simple_definition: Shipping a machine before all factory testing is done so the customer gets it sooner; final acceptance happens at the customer's site.
technical_definition: ASML practice of skipping some factory testing; revenue is deferred until site acceptance test when FAT acceptance is not proven.

simple_definition: An upgrade installed on a lithography machine already in a customer's factory to make it faster or more precise.
technical_definition: Post-sale system enhancement booked in ASML's installed base management (service and field option) revenue, e.g. NXE:3800E upgrades in 2025.

simple_definition: Using computer models to pre-distort the patterns on a mask so they print correctly on the wafer.
technical_definition: Algorithms and process models (e.g. OPC) that optimise reticle patterns and process windows for given lithography conditions.

simple_definition: An older lithography machine that is reconditioned and resold, often to makers of mature chips.
technical_definition: Pre-owned scanner/stepper resold after refurbishment; reported separately by ASML (used systems) and Nikon (refurbished units).

simple_definition: How much lithography (and spending on it) a chipmaker needs for each wafer it makes; it rises as chips get more advanced.
technical_definition: ASML term for litho exposures or litho spend per wafer start; a driver in its 2030 scenarios.

simple_definition: Everything a fab uses up while building circuits on a wafer: the wafer itself, masks, light-sensitive coatings, gases, chemicals, metal targets and polishing slurries.
technical_definition: SEMI segment covering silicon, SOI, photomasks, photoresist, photoresist ancillaries, gases, chemicals, sputtering targets and CMP; US$45.8bn in 2025 (SEMI MMDS).

simple_definition: Materials used to house, protect and connect a finished chip, such as substrates, lead frames, wires and plastic moulding.
technical_definition: SEMI segment covering leadframes, substrates, bonding wire, die attach, mold compounds, encapsulants, ceramic packages and other; US$27.4bn in 2025.

simple_definition: The helper chemicals used with photoresist: developers, thinners, rinses, strippers and coatings.
technical_definition: SEMI fab-materials segment separate from photoresist; includes developers, edge-bead removers, strippers and anti-reflective coatings. TECHCET separates 'ancillaries' and 'extensions' (hardmasks, ARCs).

simple_definition: The polishing liquids and pads used to grind each layer of a chip perfectly flat.
technical_definition: Slurries (abrasive particles such as silica, alumina or ceria in chemistry) and polishing pads for chemical-mechanical planarization; TECHCET: ~US$3.4bn in 2024 (slurry ~US$2bn, pads US$1.39bn).

simple_definition: A block of very pure metal that a machine blasts with ions so that thin metal films land on the wafer.
technical_definition: High-purity metal or alloy source for physical vapour deposition; a SEMI fab-materials segment ('Targets').

simple_definition: The ultra-pure gases a fab uses: large volumes of nitrogen and hydrogen, plus small volumes of special gases for etching, deposition and doping.
technical_definition: TECHCET splits bulk gases (N2, H2, O2, Ar, often generated on site) and specialty gases (e.g. WF6, NF3); US$6.34bn forecast for 2025.

simple_definition: Ultra-clean acids, bases and solvents used to clean and etch wafers between steps.
technical_definition: Ultra-high-purity (UHP) acids (HF, H2SO4, HNO3), bases and solvents plus formulated cleans and post-etch residue removers; TECHCET: US$5.44bn in 2025.

simple_definition: A silicon wafer with a thin buried insulating layer, used for some fast or low-power chips.
technical_definition: Engineered substrate with a buried oxide under a thin silicon device layer; a separate SEMI fab-materials segment from bulk silicon.

simple_definition: A thin metal frame that holds a chip and provides its pins in many low-cost packages.
technical_definition: Stamped or etched copper-alloy frame to which the die is attached and wire-bonded; a SEMI packaging-materials segment.

simple_definition: The hard plastic poured around a chip to protect it.
technical_definition: Epoxy-based encapsulation material for transfer or compression moulding; SEMI packaging-materials segment; Resonac lists it as a back-end product.

simple_definition: SEMI's paid dataset that tracks how much money is spent on chipmaking materials, by type and region.
technical_definition: SEMI subscription giving annual revenue with 10 years of history and a two-year forecast, quarterly updates, seven regions; public figures come only from SEMI press releases.

simple_definition: A gas company builds a plant next to the fab and pipes gas straight in under a long contract.
technical_definition: Linde: on-site contracts are total-requirement contracts typically 10-20 years with minimum purchase and price escalation; merchant bulk contracts usually 3-7 years.

simple_definition: The machines inside a chip factory that build circuits on the silicon wafer, such as printing, depositing, etching and measuring tools.
technical_definition: SEMI segment comprising wafer processing equipment, mask/reticle equipment and fab facilities equipment; excludes test and assembly & packaging (back-end) equipment.

simple_definition: The dollar value of chipmaking machines that equipment makers report having invoiced, added up by the region they were sold into.
technical_definition: Monthly billings submitted by SEMI and SEAJ member equipment companies (95+), aggregated into seven regions and 22-24 segments in the WWSEMS report; an association statistic, not audited revenue.

simple_definition: How much Japanese equipment companies sell worldwide in a fiscal year, wherever their customers are.
technical_definition: SEAJ series of domestic and overseas sales by Japanese manufacturers incl. overseas subsidiaries, fiscal year April-March, in yen; distinct from 'Japanese market billing' (sales into Japan by all makers).

simple_definition: A machine linked to the lithography scanner that spreads light-sensitive coating on the wafer before printing and develops it afterwards.
technical_definition: Photoresist processing equipment that coats, bakes and develops resist; for EUV and ArF immersion it is supplied almost entirely by Tokyo Electron and Screen.

simple_definition: Machines that check wafers during manufacturing for defects and measure whether features have the right size, so problems are caught early.
technical_definition: Wafer and reticle inspection, review and metrology tools plus analytics software; KLA is the leading supplier, with Applied Materials, ASML, Hitachi High-Tech, Onto and Lasertec as competitors.

simple_definition: Polishing a wafer flat with a slurry and pad between layers so the next layer can be built evenly.
technical_definition: Combined chemical etching and mechanical abrasion step used to planarize dielectric and metal layers; a distinct tool category in which Chinese firms held ~12.6% share in 2025 per CSET.

simple_definition: The part of a total market that a company's products can actually address.
technical_definition: For equipment makers, the share of WFE spending in tool categories where the vendor offers products (e.g. Lam: low-30% of WFE in 2025).

simple_definition: The specific machine and recipe a chipmaker officially chooses for one step in making a chip; once chosen it is rarely changed for that product.
technical_definition: A qualified production process/tool selection for a given application and node; winning PORs drives equipment share because fabs generally keep qualified tools for that node.

simple_definition: A foundry charges a set price for each finished silicon wafer it makes to a customer's design, no matter how many working chips are on it.
technical_definition: Foundry pricing basis in which volume-production revenue is the number of finished wafers shipped times a negotiated per-wafer price for the applicable design/process, adjusted by volume rebates and yield adjustments (GlobalFoundries 20-F).

simple_definition: A credit a foundry gives back to a customer when fewer good chips come off the wafers than agreed.
technical_definition: Variable consideration in foundry contracts, refundable via credit note, that reduces wafer revenue when yields fall below contractual levels; accrued against receivables.

simple_definition: A penalty a customer pays if it buys less than the minimum volume it promised in a long-term supply deal.
technical_definition: Fee under an LTA with minimum volume requirements, estimated as variable consideration and recognised with wafer revenue over the agreement term when not constrained.

simple_definition: The seller books the whole sale at one moment, usually when the goods are shipped or delivered.
technical_definition: Under ASC 606 / IFRS 15, revenue recognised when control of a good transfers at a single point (shipment, delivery, acceptance or licence delivery). Used for wafers (TSMC, GF), chips, tools, spare parts and delivered IP licences.

simple_definition: The seller books revenue gradually while it does the work or while the customer uses the service, instead of all at once.
technical_definition: Revenue recognised as a performance obligation is satisfied over a period - e.g. OSAT services and photomasks (custom output with no alternative use and a right to payment for work done), time-based EDA licences, service contracts and IP subscriptions.
where_used: OSAT, mask maker, EDA, equipment service revenue notes

simple_definition: Money a company expects to earn again and again from the same customers, such as subscriptions, support fees or royalties.
technical_definition: Company-defined (non-GAAP) category. Cadence: revenue recognised over time plus short-term renewable software and committed-spend arrangements (80% in FY2025). PDF Solutions: scheduled items plus historically re-occurring volume items (94% in 2025). Definitions differ across companies.

simple_definition: Revenue a software or IP company books in full at the start of a deal, such as a hardware sale or a perpetual licence.
technical_definition: Cadence's term for revenue recognised at a point in time, mainly hardware, individual IP licences and some software licences with a term over one year.

simple_definition: Signed business a company has not yet delivered and so has not yet counted as revenue.
technical_definition: ASC 606 disclosure of the transaction price allocated to unsatisfied obligations; EDA and IP vendors usually exclude future sales-based royalties (Synopsys US$11.4bn; Arm US$2.07bn).

simple_definition: A deal where a chip designer commits to spend a fixed amount with an EDA vendor and picks the specific tools later.
technical_definition: Non-cancellable commitment of a fixed dollar amount over a period, drawn down against a product list; Synopsys reported US$2.0bn in its backlog at 31 Oct 2025; Cadence describes similar non-cancelable commitments.

simple_definition: A licensee pays a lump sum up front to reduce or replace future per-chip royalties.
technical_definition: Arrangement in IP licensing (Arm) where prepaid or minimum royalty commitments are treated as fixed consideration and recognised as licensing revenue at a point in time.

simple_definition: A licence that lets a chip company design its own processor cores that follow Arm's instruction set, rather than use Arm-designed cores.
technical_definition: Arm licence to architecture IP including future version extensions over contracts of 3 to 20 years; consideration is allocated between available architecture and deferred future extensions.

simple_definition: A fee a fab-software vendor earns that goes up or down with how many wafers its customer produces.
technical_definition: PDF Solutions' volume-based revenue tied to customers' wafer manufacturing volumes, recognised in the usage period and accrued from estimates before customer reports.

simple_definition: A chipmaker pays a tool maker to hold a place in its production schedule for a machine it will receive later.
technical_definition: ASML contract term giving ASML a right to payment for systems through reservation of a production slot and/or on delivery, with the balance on final acceptance; most contracts also require a down payment.

simple_definition: A multi-year framework deal in which a chipmaker agrees to buy a number of tools at negotiated discounts.
technical_definition: ASML framework agreement covering up to five years with multiple performance obligations (systems, options, installation, warranties), discounts, free goods/credits; individual sales orders draw down on it. KLA also uses volume purchase agreements with credits and incentives.

simple_definition: When a chip company's own factory unit 'sells' wafers to its own product units at prices meant to look like market prices.
technical_definition: Intel Foundry records intersegment wafer and back-end service revenue from Intel Products at prices intended to approximate market pricing; external customers were US$307m of its 2025 revenue.

simple_definition: A right that lets a distributor send back slow-selling chips to the maker in exchange for others.
technical_definition: Distributor right to return a portion of inventory for other products; treated by chipmakers (Microchip) as variable consideration estimated with the expected-value method.

simple_definition: Whether a distributor books the full selling price as its revenue (it owns the goods) or only its fee (it just arranges the sale).
technical_definition: ASC 606 test: principal if it controls the goods (inventory risk, pricing discretion, fulfilment), recording gross revenue; agent if it arranges supply by another party, recording the net fee (Avnet, Arrow).

simple_definition: Money a chip company pays partners to promote its products, which it counts as a reduction of its sales.
technical_definition: Partner payments earmarked for market-segment development; NVIDIA accounts for MDFs and reseller rebates as reductions to revenue.

simple_definition: Money a customer pays a chipmaker up front to guarantee supply, returned if it buys the promised amount.
technical_definition: Microchip LTSA (3-5 years): upfront deposit plus minimum purchase commitments in exchange for assured supply; deposit returned if commitments met, otherwise retained and recognised as revenue.

example: SIA/BCG estimated the US 10-year TCO at about 30% above Taiwan, South Korea or Singapore.
simple_definition: Everything it costs to build a chip factory and run it for ten years, minus the money governments give back.
technical_definition: In SIA/BCG usage: upfront capital expenditure (land, construction, equipment) plus ten years of cash operating expenses (labour, utilities, materials, taxes), minus government incentives.
where_used: Fab-location cost comparisons and subsidy debates (SIA/BCG 2020, BCG 2023)

aliases: gross margin dilution from overseas fabs
example: TSMC guided 2-3% dilution in early years widening to 3-4% later.
simple_definition: How much a chipmaker's overall profit margin drops because its new factories abroad cost more to run than its home factories.
technical_definition: Percentage-point reduction in consolidated gross margin attributed by the company to ramping fabs outside its home base (TSMC: Arizona, Kumamoto, Dresden), reflecting higher cost, smaller scale and start-up depreciation.

simple_definition: A group of several chip factories built side by side so they can share buildings, power, water and staff.
technical_definition: TSMC's site model in which six or seven 300mm fab phases share central facility plants; IC Knowledge estimates it cuts construction cost by about 25% versus a stand-alone fab.
where_used: TSMC Taiwan sites (Fab 12, 14, 15, 18) and the planned Arizona cluster

simple_definition: How many blank wafers a factory begins processing each month; the standard measure of fab size.
technical_definition: Monthly count of wafers entering the fab process, usually stated in 300mm (12-inch) or 200mm-equivalent wafers; used to size fabs and compare capex per unit of capacity (e.g. capex per 1,000 wpm).
where_used: Fab announcements, government approvals, cost models

aliases: useful life of machinery and equipment
simple_definition: The number of years over which a chipmaker spreads the purchase cost of its tools in its accounts; a longer life makes each wafer look cheaper.
technical_definition: Estimated useful life used for straight-line depreciation of production equipment; TSMC uses 5 years, Intel moved certain tools from 5 to 8 years in 2023, and IC Knowledge models default to 5 years for equipment, 10 for building systems and 15 for buildings.

example: NVIDIA is SIC 3674; Lam Research is SIC 3559.
simple_definition: A four-digit US government number that says what kind of business a company is in; the SEC still tags every filer with one.
technical_definition: Standard Industrial Classification code; replaced by NAICS for US statistics in 1997 but retained by SEC EDGAR to describe filers and assign review offices.

simple_definition: The permanent ID number the SEC gives every company or person that files with it.
technical_definition: Central Index Key: 10-digit identifier (with leading zeros) used in EDGAR URLs and APIs, e.g. data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK##########.json.

simple_definition: A way of tagging each number in a financial report so computers can read it directly.
technical_definition: eXtensible Business Reporting Language, XML-based; required by the SEC since 2009 (now mostly inline XBRL); facts tied to US-GAAP or IFRS taxonomies. Also used by EDINET and DART.

simple_definition: The yearly report that foreign companies listed in the US file with the SEC, in English.
technical_definition: Annual report/registration form for foreign private issuers under the Exchange Act; due within four months after fiscal year-end; filed on EDGAR.

simple_definition: A big US-listed company that must file its annual report fastest (within 60 days).
technical_definition: SEC Rule 12b-2 filer category determining 10-K deadlines (60/75/90 days) and shown in EDGAR submissions metadata ('category').

simple_definition: Taiwan-listed companies must publish last month's sales by the 10th of each month, which gives an early look at chip demand.
technical_definition: Monthly operating revenue (consolidated under IFRS) input into MOPS before the 10th of the following month under Securities and Exchange Act Art. 36; unaudited. Local-language name(s): 月營收.

simple_definition: Taiwan's official website where listed companies post their financial reports, monthly sales and important news.
technical_definition: Market Observation Post System run by TWSE and TPEx under FSC supervision; English version e-MOPS. Local-language name(s): 公開資訊觀測站.

simple_definition: A Taiwan trading board for companies not yet fully listed; many young chip firms trade there first.
technical_definition: Taipei Exchange's emerging stock market (興櫃); stocks classified by the same industry groups as TWSE/TPEx. Local-language name(s): 興櫃.

simple_definition: South Korea's government website where companies publish their official filings.
technical_definition: Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer System run by the Financial Supervisory Service; OpenDART API (40-character key) gives XML filings, XBRL financials and company industry codes. Local-language name(s): 전자공시.

simple_definition: Japan's government website where companies file their official annual and half-year reports.
technical_definition: FSA's electronic disclosure system under the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act; API v2 with key; documents viewable for about 10 years.

simple_definition: The main yearly report a Japanese listed company files with the regulator, similar to a US 10-K.
technical_definition: 有価証券報告書 (yūka shōken hōkokusho) filed on EDINET under the FIEA; statutory viewing period 5 years plus 5-year extension. Local-language name(s): 有価証券報告書.

simple_definition: A Chinese website approved by the securities regulator where listed companies publish official announcements.
technical_definition: 巨潮资讯网 (www.cninfo.com.cn), a CSRC-designated information-disclosure website. Local-language name(s): 巨潮资讯网.

simple_definition: Shares of mainland Chinese companies traded in yuan on the Shanghai, Shenzhen or Beijing exchanges.
technical_definition: RMB-denominated ordinary shares listed on mainland exchanges; disclosure in Chinese via CSRC-appointed media.

example: CXMT listed on the STAR Market in 2026.
simple_definition: A Shanghai stock board for technology companies; it holds the largest group of listed Chinese chip companies.
technical_definition: Sci-Tech Innovation Board of the Shanghai Stock Exchange, launched 13 June 2019; 588 companies and 119 IC companies as of June 2025. Local-language name(s): 科创板.

simple_definition: Hang Seng's system for sorting Hong Kong-listed companies by industry; it has a semiconductor sector.
technical_definition: Hang Seng Industry Classification System: 12 industries, 31 sectors, 114 subsectors; semiconductors 703010, semiconductor equipment & materials 703020; revenue-based.

simple_definition: A private industry-sorting scheme from MSCI and S&P used by investors; chip firms are in 4530 'Semiconductors & Semiconductor Equipment'.
technical_definition: Global Industry Classification Standard; sub-industries 45301010 Semiconductor Materials & Equipment and 45301020 Semiconductors; 60% revenue rule; licensed data.

simple_definition: Hong Kong listing rules that let specialist tech companies, including some chip firms, list before they have big revenues.
technical_definition: HKEX Main Board Chapter 18C (Specialist Technology Companies); pre-commercial issuers carry a 'P' marker in their stock names.

simple_definition: Filings that tell the public when big shareholders or directors buy or sell a Hong Kong-listed company's shares.
technical_definition: Notices under Part XV of the Securities and Futures Ordinance, filed electronically via HKEX's DION system since 3 July 2017 and published on HKEXnews.

simple_definition: A Japanese IPO route that lets a company file its offering document before the exchange approves the listing, to sound out investors earlier.
technical_definition: Pre-approval securities registration statement (承認前届出書) introduced October 2023; Kioxia (Dec 2024) was the first IPO to use it. Local-language name(s): 承認前届出書.

simple_definition: A complete count and list of all companies in an industry, not only the famous ones.
technical_definition: Enumeration of every entity per role and country, combining official classification lists, filing-text searches, association directories and government lists, deduplicated by legal entity.

simple_definition: A non-US company listed in the US that follows lighter SEC rules, such as yearly Form 20-F instead of quarterly 10-Qs.
technical_definition: SEC status under Exchange Act Rule 3b-4; files 20-F annually (within four months) and 6-K for interim information.

simple_definition: A report Japanese listed companies file after the first half of their year; it replaced the legal quarterly report in 2024.
technical_definition: 半期報告書 under amended FIEA Art. 24-5 from 1 April 2024, due within 45 days (60 days for some companies). Local-language name(s): 半期報告書.
